answer:
To cap concurrent API calls in `promptfoo eval`, use the `-j` or `--max-concurrency` flag. The docs describe it as "Maximum number of concurrent API calls" ["`-j, --max-concurrency <number>` ... Maximum number of concurrent API calls" [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]].

For example, the OSWorld guide runs with a concurrency of 1:

```bash
promptfoo eval -c promptfooconfig.yaml --no-cache \
  --filter-metadata app=libreoffice_calc --max-concurrency 1 \
  -o osworld-libreoffice-calc.json
```

This command appears in "promptfoo eval -c promptfooconfig.yaml --no-cache --filter-metadata app=libreoffice_calc --max-concurrency 1" [promptfoo/site/docs/guides/evaluate-osworld-with-inspect.md].

The provided excerpts don't show the default concurrency value, or whether the setting can also be placed in `promptfooconfig.yaml`. I don't know those details from this context. Also, `redteam run` has a separate `-j, --max-concurrency` option, but that applies to red team runs, not to `eval`.
